target_customer: Insured patients with chronic conditions who benefit from dietitian care; revenue comes from insurers
problem: Poor nutrition drives chronic disease, yet fewer than 1 percent of insured Americans use their dietitian benefit because of provider shortage and expensive cash-pay options.
business_model: Telehealth dietitian visits billed to health insurance

founders.name: Aidan Dewar
founders.background_notes: Childhood friend of Perkins; motivated by his own migraines per TechCrunch.

founders.name: Sam Perkins
founders.background_notes: Motivated by his own IBS per TechCrunch; TechCrunch says Liu became close friends with him at Princeton.

investors: J.P. Morgan Private Capital Growth Equity Partners

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly care delivery and insurance billing operations; software is a scheduling, EHR and billing stack.

defensibility.rationale: Payer contracts and credentialed in-network dietitians are slow to replicate, though the service itself is copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the wedge; Nourish kept raising through Series C.

market_need_then: The launch post says more than half of Americans have a diet related chronic condition and most insured people have dietitian coverage but fewer than 1 percent use it.

branding.domain_note: The company site is now nourish.com (blog links moved from usenourish.com); acquisition details not found.

brand_strength.rationale: A generic dictionary word shared by many unrelated Nourish brands, with no brand press found; growth came from insurance coverage, not brand.

outcome_analysis: Nourish built a telehealth dietitian network paid by insurers and raised 8 million dollars seed in January 2023, 35 million Series A in March 2024, 70 million Series B in April 2025 and 100 million Series C in May 2026. Founder motivation from their own chronic conditions and a large unused insurance benefit gave a clear wedge, and in-network payer coverage makes patient cost near zero.
notes: Totals differ by source (115 million after Series B per the company; 215 million after Series C per press; ZoomInfo 113 million). TechCrunch implies an earlier 1.3 million dollars (9.3 total minus 8 seed), not recorded as a round. Series A and C details come from search summaries and the company blog; the Series C page itself was not opened. The launch post and TechCrunch name no competitors; directory lists naming Oviva, Foodsmart and others are undated so the competitor list is empty and takeover risk names Foodsmart and Real Appeal only from a current profile. Seed date is the TechCrunch article date.
